control_config_generation_snapshot.note: Recorded so a reader can see which configuration was in force at the freeze, and NOT as a freeze constraint. The control-config generation is designed to move -- a repository, routing or listener change MUST move it -- so treating a changed config digest as schema drift would be a wrong-subject error. The freeze verifier deliberately does not check it.

enforcement: The generation 2 artifacts live on the same drvfs mount as generation 1, which does not carry file modes, so write-once cannot be enforced by permission here either. Enforcement is DIGEST COMPARISON ONLY -- detective, not preventive -- through bin/fsc2-verify-freeze.sh, which re-hashes every artifact above and refuses on any drift. This is a real limit, recorded rather than assumed away. The one thing that DID move to a filesystem with real modes is the private mutable runtime home, because the upstream listener registrar requires an exact 0700.
freeze_ordering: FROZEN BEFORE any generation 2 envelope was compiled or emitted. No fm-sol-control/v2 generation 2 request exists: emitting one is a separately authorized lane and the emitter refuses without that lane's token. The watched-red harness was run against these exact frozen bytes AFTER this record was written; the authoring iterations that preceded the freeze are pre-freeze churn, not mutation of a frozen artifact.

supersedes.disposition: Generation 1 stays frozen, published and untouched. The completed NO_ANSWER transaction on issue #1 was emitted under it and is never revalidated under generation 2: an immutable historical record is not a defect to retrofit.
